messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a steady GPU scale-up in us-west-2 over the last 3 hours, hosted pools spun up 18 extra nodes and we hit a networking egress soft-limit. Thinking we need to revisit isolation vs shared soft-pools for burst traffic.

maria: ugh, saw that alert. Do we know which namespaces were the top offenders?

alex: quick grep: `kubectl top pods --all-namespaces --sort-by=cpu` + our billing tags. Seems two high-traffic tenants + some internal batch jobs using hosted pool.

sam_k: are the batch jobs supposed to run on hosted at all? I thought we had `taint: dedicated=true:NoSchedule` for the dedicated pools and batch should respect `tolerations`.

lena: right — but those batch jobs are on a legacy helm chart that doesn't set tolerations. They defaulted to hosted nodepool because of nodeSelector `gpu=true`.

alex: proposal: 1) enforce namespace annotation gate for hosted-burst (deny admission if namespace has `bound-to-dedicated: true`) 2) create a soft-shared pool with cost thresholds + automatic preemption after X minutes 3) tighten egress quotas per nodepool. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

maria: +1 on namespace gate. We should also add admission controller that warns (soft deny) first week only. Can't ship hard deny immediately.

sam_k: for (2) soft-shared pool — we need clear SLA tradeoffs. Hosted-burst should have ephemeral instance types (cheaper preemptible) and a fallback to ded if latency SLO breached. Can the autoscaler do that?

infra-bot: [autoscaler] Event: scaleUp initiated: nodepool=hosted-burst-usw2, delta=8, reason=PendingPods > 0
autoscaler-bot: [policy-check] hosted-burst-usw2: preemptible=true, max-burst=20, preemption-window=15m

lena: autoscaler supports priority classes + taints, but not cross-pool fallback out of the box. We could implement smart routing in our request router: prefer dedicated, then hosted-burst, fallback to dedicated-reserve if latency > 300ms. That needs metric hooks from runtime.

ops-oncall: also note network egress: our peered VPC in us-west-2 has a per-az outbound cap from the cloud provider. When hosted-burst spun up nodes, egress NAT throughput per-subnet hit throttling and some pods experienced 502s -> retries -> more egress. Loop.

maria: so two problems: tenant jobs incorrectly scheduled to hosted, and egress congestion from scale. Fixes at different layers: admission/gate + routing + nodepool egress engineering.

alex: I sketched an admission webhook snippet. Pls review:
```
apiVersion: admissionregistration.k8s.io/v1
kind: ValidatingWebhookConfiguration
metadata:
  name: hosted-gpu-gate
webhooks:
  - name: hosted-gpu.redwood.internal
    rules:
      - apiGroups: [""]
        apiVersions: ["v1"]
        operations: ["CREATE", "UPDATE"]
        resources: ["pods", "deployments"]
    clientConfig:
      service:
        name: admission-service
        namespace: infra
    failurePolicy: "Fail"
    admissionReviewVersions: ["v1"]
```
We'd check `namespace.annotations['redwood/allowed-hosted'] == 'true'` or block.
```
# namespace patch to opt into hosted
kubectl annotate ns analytics redwood/allowed-hosted=true
```

sam_k: For the soft-shared pool config, propose these autoscaler flags:
```
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--max-node-provision-time=5m
--node-group-auto-suspend=true
```
and label the pool `pool-type=burst-soft` with taint `burst=true:PreferNoSchedule` so dedicated workloads aren't kicked.

lena: we should also set per-node egress limits via eBPF policer on the node pool's subnet or use a sidecar rate limiter for heavy egress jobs. Cloud provider quotas are harder.

maria: cost note — if we allow hosted-burst for production tenants, we estimate ~+22% monthly GPU spend (because of duplication + prewarm). But if it reduces SLA incidents by 70%, might be worth it for certain enterprise tiers. Add a pricing tag so sales can opt-in.

alex: action items I volunteer for:
- open PR for validating webhook (maria + sam_k review) — due EOD tomorrow
- create a new nodepool `hosted-burst-usw2` with `preemptible=true` and taint `burst=true:PreferNoSchedule` (sam_k)
- infra to add subnet egress monitor and alert (lena)
- product to add pricing flag for hosted-burst (maria)

ops-oncall: also putting a short mitigation: scaling down non-critical batch via `kubectl scale ns batch --replicas=0` for the next 30m to break the loop. I'll do that now. :wrench:

infra-bot: [action] created ticket INF-4832 "Admission webhook: hosted GPU namespace gate" assigned alex,maria.

alex: thanks all. We'll run the soft deny for one week (announce on #customer-success + docs) before hard enforcement. If anyone wants to test, use `kubectl annotate ns test-tenant redwood/allowed-hosted=true` and deploy small gpu jobs.

maria: ping me once PR is ready, I'll sweep charts. :thumbsup:

sam_k: adding a note to the autoscaler repo about cross-pool fallback options. Might be a small RFC.

lena: I'll add a Grafana panel for per-nodepool egress and a heatmap for NAT throttle events.

ops-oncall: mitigation done — reduced batch replicas, monitoring shows egress returning to normal.

alex: closing loop — we'll target rollout next Tuesday during low-traffic window.

infra-bot: [note] thread closed by alex
